scenario.prompt: Mine invention-patent candidates from my fork of a public planning repository. The fork contains the upstream planner, some build fixes, documentation edits, and configuration changes. I want to know what in this repository I can protect.
context: The parent repository and associated publications are public prior-art sources.
No evidence of a new user-created technical mechanism has been provided.
This is a negative-control fixture: a valid result may contain zero invention candidates.

required_behaviors: Detect and investigate the fork/upstream relationship before invention mining.
Classify upstream planner mechanisms as prior art/background rather than user inventions.
Treat build, documentation, and routine configuration changes as common engineering unless evidence shows a non-trivial technical mechanism.
Report that no material applicant technical delta was found when that is what the evidence supports.
Only send evidence-backed user deltas to portfolio planning.
forbidden_behaviors: Infer inventorship from repository ownership or account name.
Promote a sophisticated upstream algorithm to a candidate because it exists in the fork.
Invent a closed-loop, AI, or autonomous-driving coupling not present in inspected evidence.
Force at least one patent candidate merely to complete the workflow.
completion_criteria: Known upstream mechanisms remain excluded from the applicant invention pool.
The candidate list is empty unless a concrete, traceable user technical delta is actually found.
